intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day longtail boat tour around the stunning Phi Phi archipelago, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, exploring Viking Cave, and swimming at Monkey Beach. Witness dramatic limestone karsts and vibrant coral reefs teeming with tropical fish.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Crawl
experiences.description: Dive into Bangkok's legendary street food scene at Yaowarat Road (Chinatown), sampling pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, tom yum soup, and fresh oyster omelets from bustling roadside stalls. Join a guided walking tour or explore independently through the aromatic alleyways after dark.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Sunset Beach Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle a sea kayak along Koh Lanta's serene western coastline, exploring hidden sea caves, mangrove tunnels, and secluded coves. Time your return to witness a breathtaking Andaman Sea sunset painting the sky in vivid oranges and purples from the water.
experiences.location: Klong Dao Beach, Koh Lanta, Krabi Province

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Cooking Class & Morning Market Tour
experiences.description: Start the day at a vibrant local fresh market selecting exotic ingredients, then learn to prepare five authentic Northern Thai dishes including khao soi, green curry, and som tum under the guidance of a local chef. Take home a recipe booklet and the skills to recreate the flavors of Thailand.

experiences.name: Similan Islands Liveaboard Snorkel & Dive Day Trip
experiences.description: Board a speedboat to the world-renowned Similan Islands National Park, one of Thailand's most pristine marine environments. Snorkel or dive among whale sharks, manta rays, and colorful reef fish around dramatic granite boulders and untouched white sand beaches accessible only by boat.
experiences.location: Similan Islands National Park, Phang Nga Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive on Flight UA at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange budget transfer (shared shuttle or public bus) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Grab a quick late-night snack from a nearby 7-Eleven or street vendor if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On flight
meals.lunch: On flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snack (7-Eleven pad kra pao cup noodles or Thai snacks) — ~฿30-60

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival simple. Have hotel address written in Thai to show taxi or shuttle driver. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport for immediate needs. Budget tip: shared airport shuttles are significantly cheaper than private taxis.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to orient yourself. Explore the immediate beach area, watch local fishermen, and soak in your first Thai morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~฿100-200/day) and explore the local area around the resort. Visit a nearby local market to pick up fresh tropical fruit (mango, rambutan, dragon fruit) and get a feel for the neighborhood. Scout out street food stalls for future meals.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest beach promenade or night market for dinner. Watch the sunset from the beach, then browse street food stalls for a classic Thai dinner spread.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast if included, or local coffee shop — Thai-style toast with pandan jam and Thai iced tea (~฿50-80)
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from local market + mango sticky rice from a street stall (~฿60-80)
meals.dinner: Night market street food — pad thai, grilled skewers, papaya salad, and fresh coconut (~฿120-180 total)

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to recover from jet lag. Use this day to get your bearings, find your favorite local food spots, and plan the week ahead. Download the Grab app for affordable local transport.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise beach walk. Enjoy the quiet morning on the beach before the crowds arrive. Find a local breakfast spot and try khao tom (Thai rice porridge) or jok (congee) — a classic Thai morning meal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget group snorkeling trip or longtail boat tour to nearby reefs and islands. These group tours are significantly cheaper than private charters (~฿400-600 per person) and offer a great introduction to the local marine life and surrounding islands.
day_by_day.evening: Return from the boat tour and relax on the beach. Head out for street food dinner and explore any local beach bars with happy hour specials (cheap Chang or Leo beer ~฿60-80).

meals.breakfast: Local restaurant — khao tom with egg and salted fish (~฿60-80)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from a convenience store or eat at the tour's stop (~฿80-120)
meals.dinner: Beachside street food — tom yum soup, steamed rice, and grilled fish (~฿150-200)

day_by_day.notes: Book group boat tours through your guesthouse or local tour operators on the street — avoid hotel booking desks which add significant markup. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and a dry bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Explore local temples (wat) in the area. Visit a nearby Buddhist temple early morning when monks are active. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered). Witness or participate in the alms-giving ceremony if available in your area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fresh market (talat sod) to experience authentic Thai daily life. Sample local street snacks — kanom krok (coconut pancakes), tod mun pla (fish cakes), and fresh-squeezed sugarcane juice. Pick up budget souvenirs like handmade bracelets or local spices.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or assemble your own Thai meal — buy ingredients from the market (fresh herbs, vegetables, noodles) and use hostel/guesthouse kitchen facilities, or simply assemble a picnic-style dinner on the beach with market finds.

meals.breakfast: Street vendor — roti with banana and condensed milk + Thai iced coffee (~฿60-80)
meals.lunch: Fresh market snacks and samples (~฿80-100)
meals.dinner: Market-bought picnic or local Thai restaurant — green curry with rice (~฿80-120)

day_by_day.notes: October is part of the wet season in many parts of Thailand — carry a compact umbrella or rain poncho. Morning temple visits are generally drier. Check local weather forecasts daily.

day_by_day.morning: Island hopping day — depart early on a budget group island-hopping tour. Visit 2-3 nearby islands, including stops for swimming, snorkeling, and beach exploration. Look for tours that include Maya Bay, Phi Phi, or Similan-style islands depending on your location.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping tour. Enjoy lunch on one of the islands (pack your own to save money or buy from island vendors). Swim in crystal-clear waters and explore hidden lagoons and viewpoints.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon/early evening. Rest, shower, and head out for a well-deserved street food feast to celebrate a great day on the water.

meals.breakfast: Early morning — grab-and-go from 7-Eleven: banana, boiled egg, and Thai milk tea (~฿50-70)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or instant noodles from convenience store, or buy from island vendor (~฿80-150)
meals.dinner: Reward yourself at a local seafood street stall — grilled prawns, steamed clams, and jasmine rice (~฿180-250)

day_by_day.notes: Book island-hopping tours the day before for the best prices. Group tours run ~฿600-1,200 per person including boat, snorkel gear, and sometimes lunch. Avoid tours that seem extremely cheap as they may cut corners on safety. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend time on the resort's beachfront. Read, journal, or simply relax and watch the ocean. This is a buffer day to recharge mid-trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a long walk or motorbike ride along the coastal road to discover hidden beaches, local fishing villages, and scenic viewpoints. Stop at any interesting spots along the way for photos and exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Find a local Thai cooking class (budget classes run ~฿500-800 per person) or watch a Muay Thai match at a local stadium if available in your area. Both are authentic cultural experiences at budget-friendly prices.

meals.breakfast: Resort or local café — American breakfast or Thai-style eggs with toast (~฿80-120)
meals.lunch: Roadside noodle shop — kuay teow (noodle soup) with your choice of protein (~฿50-70)
meals.dinner: Cooking class meal (if joined) or local restaurant — massaman curry with roti (~฿100-150)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest days are important for budget travelers to avoid burnout. Use this day to do laundry (laundry services are very cheap in Thailand ~฿40-60/kg), recharge devices, and plan the second half of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding rental along the coastline (~฿200-400/hour). Paddle to nearby coves, sea caves, or mangrove areas for a peaceful and active morning on the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local viewpoint or hilltop for panoramic views of the surrounding islands and coast. Hike or take a motorbike to the summit. Bring water and snacks. Explore any jungle trails or nature paths in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Street food tour — dedicate the evening to systematically trying as many different Thai street foods as possible. Create a personal food challenge: try at least 5 different dishes across different stalls.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or street cart — fresh baguette with butter (Thai-French influence) and coffee (~฿60-80)
meals.lunch: Hilltop café or packed lunch from convenience store (~฿80-120)
meals.dinner: Street food tour extravaganza — som tam, moo ping (grilled pork skewers), pad see ew, mango sticky rice, and Thai tea (~฿150-200 for everything)

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rentals are widely available at most Thai beaches. Always wear a life jacket. For viewpoint hikes, start before noon to avoid the hottest part of the day and potential afternoon rain showers.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a different nearby island — take a local ferry or longtail boat to a neighboring island for a change of scenery. Choose a less-touristy island for a more authentic experience and lower prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the chosen island on foot or by rented bicycle. Visit local villages, find secluded beaches, and interact with local residents. Look for a local lunch spot away from tourist areas for the most authentic and affordable food.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the main island by late afternoon. Sunset beach session followed by dinner at a highly-rated local restaurant (still budget-friendly) to treat yourself mid-week.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before ferry — convenience store rice balls or Thai-style omelet (~฿50-80)
meals.lunch: Local island restaurant away from tourist strip — fried rice with seafood (~฿80-120)
meals.dinner: Slightly nicer local restaurant — whole grilled fish with garlic and herbs, steamed vegetables, jasmine rice (~฿200-280)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules vary — check return times carefully to avoid being stranded on a smaller island overnight. Carry cash as smaller islands may not have ATMs. Bring sunscreen, insect repellent, and a power bank.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local elephant sanctuary or ethical wildlife experience if available in your region (~฿1,500-2,500 for ethical sanctuaries — worth the splurge). Avoid any venues offering elephant riding. Alternatively, visit a local botanical garden or nature reserve.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning excursion, relax at the beach. Try beach volleyball with other travelers, build sandcastles, or simply swim and float in the warm Thai waters.
day_by_day.evening: Night market exploration — find the biggest local night market and spend the evening browsing stalls, trying street food, shopping for budget souvenirs, and enjoying live street performances.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before excursion — Thai porridge with century egg (~฿60-80)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch for the sanctuary or eat at their café (~฿100-150)
meals.dinner: Night market feast — mix of various stalls: satay, spring rolls, pad thai, fresh fruit shake (~฿120-180)

day_by_day.notes: Always research elephant sanctuaries thoroughly before booking. Legitimate ethical sanctuaries do not offer riding, shows, or chains. The higher price is a reflection of proper animal care. This is considered a worthy splurge on a budget trip.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — rent snorkel gear (~฿100-150) and explore the reef directly from the beach. Many Thai beaches have excellent snorkeling accessible without a boat. Look for colorful fish, sea turtles, and coral formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Thai massage school or budget massage parlor for a traditional Thai massage (~฿200-300/hour). This is significantly cheaper than resort spa prices and often equally good quality. Follow with a foot massage (~฿150/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachside bar during happy hour (2-for-1 deals are common, ~฿100-150 per drink). Then head to a local restaurant for dinner and chat with other budget travelers about tips and recommendations.

meals.breakfast: Beachside café — acai bowl or smoothie bowl (~฿120-180) as a slightly indulgent treat
meals.lunch: Beach shack — fresh coconut, grilled corn, and fried chicken (~฿100-150)
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant — yellow curry with chicken and roti (~฿120-160)

day_by_day.notes: Day 10 is intentionally relaxed and self-indulgent — massage, beach, cocktails. Budget travelers often skip self-care, but affordable Thai massages make this very accessible. Tip your massage therapist ~฿50-100.

day_by_day.morning: Final island-hopping adventure — book a different route or tour than Day 5 to see new islands and snorkeling spots. Focus on less-visited islands for a quieter, more pristine experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island exploration. Visit a local fishing village on one of the islands to see traditional Thai island life. Buy freshly caught seafood directly from fishermen for an incredibly fresh and cheap meal.
day_by_day.evening: Beach bonfire or social evening at the resort or nearby beach bar. Share travel stories with fellow budget travelers. This is a great time to swap tips about other destinations in Southeast Asia.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go — Thai-style sandwich and cold brew coffee (~฿80-100)
meals.lunch: Freshly caught seafood bought from island fishermen, grilled simply on the beach (~฿150-200)
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant — seafood platter to share with new travel friends (~฿200-300 per person)

day_by_day.notes: On the second-to-last full day, consider doing any last-minute shopping for souvenirs, gifts, or Thai products to bring home. Local markets offer the best prices — avoid airport shops.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk — wake up early for one last sunrise over the ocean. Reflect on the trip, take photos, and enjoy the peaceful early morning. Swim one last time in the warm Thai waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack and organize luggage. Do a final check of the room. Spend remaining Thai baht wisely — buy local snacks and packaged Thai products (curry pastes, dried mango, coconut candies) to bring home as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell street food dinner — revisit your favorite street food stalls from the trip. Order all your favorite dishes one last time. Take photos of the food and the vendors who made your trip delicious.

meals.breakfast: Favorite local breakfast spot — one last khao tom or pad kra pao with fried egg (~฿80-120)
meals.lunch: Light lunch — fresh spring rolls and papaya salad (~฿80-100)
meals.dinner: Farewell feast at the best street food market — order generously, it's your last night (~฿200-280)

day_by_day.notes: Use any remaining baht on food, tips for hotel staff, and last-minute souvenirs. Keep enough cash for transport to the airport and any departure taxes. Check flight details and set multiple alarms for an early departure if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — wake up early depending on flight time. Enjoy a last Thai breakfast if time permits. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange budget airport transfer (Grab, shared shuttle, or public bus).
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to the airport. Arrive at least 2-3 hours before departure for international flights. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Thai snacks or gifts. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, islands, and street food.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Thailand with incredible memories, a full photo gallery, a deeper love of Thai cuisine, and a significantly lighter wallet — well spent on one of the world's greatest budget travel destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast near hotel or at airport — khao man gai (chicken rice) or airport food court (~฿80-150)
meals.lunch: Airport food court — surprisingly good and reasonably priced Thai options (~฿150-200)
meals.dinner: On the flight home

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: A 13-day budget trip to Thailand typically costs $800-1,400 USD total (excluding flights) covering accommodation, food, activities, and transport. Street food, group tours, and local transport are the keys to keeping costs low. Thailand rewards budget travelers with incredible value — you can eat like royalty on ฿300/day.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive on Flight UA at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: On flight
meals.lunch: On flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near the resort or hotel room service — try a simple bowl of Tom Kha soup or Pad See Ew from a nearby night stall if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance. Have Thai Baht ready for tips and small purchases. Confirm resort check-in for late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront to get your bearings and soak in the surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area on foot or by rented scooter. Visit the nearest beach town or village, browse local shops, and get oriented with the neighborhood. Stop by a local market to pick up snacks and essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest beach promenade or night market for your first real taste of Thai street food. Try multiple stalls and sample various dishes.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a nearby café — try Thai-style eggs with rice porridge (Jok)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near the beach — order Pad Thai or Khao Pad (Thai fried rice) for around 80–120 THB
meals.dinner: Street food night market — try Moo Ping (grilled pork skewers), Som Tum (papaya salad), and fresh coconut water

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag recovery day. Keep the pace relaxed. Exchange currency at a local bank or ATM for better rates. Pick up a local SIM card for data.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim or yoga on the beach at sunrise. Rent a kayak or paddleboard from the resort beach for a 1–2 hour session along the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day snorkeling trip departing from the local pier. Explore nearby coral reefs and marine life. Many mid-range tour operators offer this for 600–900 THB per person including equipment.
day_by_day.evening: Return to shore by late afternoon. Shower and relax, then explore a nearby beachside restaurant strip for dinner with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Beachside café — fresh fruit smoothie bowl, toast with local jam, and Thai iced coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the snorkeling boat or a beachside shack — grilled fish with sticky rice
meals.dinner: Mid-range seafood restaurant — order whole grilled fish with garlic and chili, steamed rice, and a mango sticky rice dessert (budget 350–500 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkeling trip the evening before through the resort concierge or a local tour desk. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a rash guard. October may bring some afternoon showers — carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat or ferry to a nearby island for a full-day island hopping adventure. Depart early (around 8:00–9:00 AM) to beat the crowds at the first island stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping — visit 2–3 islands in the area, including a hidden beach or lagoon if accessible. Swim, snorkel, and explore each stop for 45–60 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon. Head out for a casual evening stroll and visit a local night bazaar for shopping and street food grazing.

meals.breakfast: Quick bite at the pier before departure — fresh roti with banana and condensed milk or a savory rice dish
meals.lunch: Beach BBQ on one of the islands or a floating restaurant — grilled prawns, squid, and corn on the cob
meals.dinner: Night bazaar street food — Satay skewers, spring rolls, Pad Krapow (basil stir-fry), and Thai iced tea

day_by_day.notes: Book island hopping tour in advance — prices range from 800–1,500 THB depending on the number of islands and inclusions. Bring cash, sunscreen, a dry bag, and a change of clothes.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning at the resort. Enjoy a swim in the resort pool or the ocean. Take time to journal, read, or simply relax on the beach with a fresh coconut.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Thai cooking class (typically 1,200–1,800 THB per person). Learn to make 3–4 classic dishes including Tom Yum soup, Pad Thai, and green curry. Many classes include a market visit.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the meal you cooked at the end of the cooking class, then take a tuk-tuk or taxi to a rooftop bar or beachside lounge for sunset cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or local café — try Khao Tom (rice soup with egg and ginger) for a light Thai-style breakfast
meals.lunch: Eat what you cook during the cooking class
meals.dinner: Rooftop bar with light bites — share a cheese board or Thai tapas platter while enjoying cocktails (300–500 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance. Look for classes that include a local market tour in the morning for an enriched experience. Great for souvenirs — you'll take home the recipes!

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby national park or nature reserve. Hike a jungle trail to a viewpoint or waterfall. Depart by 8:00 AM to make the most of the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the park — swim in a natural pool at the base of a waterfall if available, or visit a scenic viewpoint for panoramic views. Return to the resort by 4:00–5:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage at a local spa (60–90 minute session for 400–700 THB). Then enjoy a quiet dinner near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Pack a breakfast from a local bakery or convenience store — banana, boiled eggs, and a coffee to go
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the national park or at a park café — fried rice, fresh fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant near the resort — try Massaman curry with roti, a green papaya salad, and steamed jasmine rice

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes for hiking. Bring insect repellent, sunscreen, and plenty of water. Check park opening hours and entrance fees in advance (usually 200–300 THB for foreigners).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — take a ferry or speedboat to a new island destination (e.g., Koh Lanta, Koh Phi Phi, or Koh Tao depending on your base location). Depart after breakfast and enjoy the scenic boat ride.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the new island, check into a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel. Drop your bags and immediately head to the beach for a swim and explore the main strip.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the island's main village or beach road. Browse handicraft shops, pick up local souvenirs, and find a great spot for dinner with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Resort or hotel breakfast before checkout — or grab a quick bite at the pier
meals.lunch: On the ferry if available, or at a beachside restaurant upon arrival — try a fresh fish burger or noodle soup
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on the new island — seafood platter for two with garlic butter prawns, grilled fish, and fried calamari (500–800 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance, especially in October which can see busy travel periods. Keep valuables in a waterproof bag during the boat transfer. Confirm accommodation on the new island before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or bicycle and explore the new island independently. Visit viewpoints, hidden beaches, and local temples at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day diving or advanced snorkeling excursion from the island's dive center. Many islands offer world-class dive sites with vibrant coral and marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the main beach area for the famous beach fire show or a beach bonfire gathering if available. Enjoy the relaxed island nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Local café on the island — try a Thai-style breakfast of rice porridge, fried egg, and fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Beachside shack during the diving break — simple fried rice or noodles with a cold Chang beer
meals.dinner: Casual beach bar dinner — BBQ skewers, som tum, sticky rice, and fresh fruit shakes

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental is approximately 200–300 THB per day. Always wear a helmet. Diving excursions range from 1,500–2,500 THB. Check PADI certification requirements if doing a dive course.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding around the island's coastline and sea caves. Many operators offer guided tours departing at sunrise for the best light and calm waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on the beach — read, swim, or simply do nothing. Visit a beachside hammock café and enjoy the island pace. Optional: visit a local fishing village for an authentic cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise around the island on a traditional longtail boat. Watch the sky turn orange and pink as the sun dips below the horizon. Return for a final dinner on the island.

meals.breakfast: Grab and go from a bakery or street vendor — banana pancake, fresh fruit, and Thai iced coffee
meals.lunch: Hammock café or beach shack — avocado toast, smoothie bowl, or a fresh coconut curry
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual beachfront restaurant — try a whole fish cooked in banana leaf, mango salad, and coconut ice cream for dessert (400–600 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunset cruises typically cost 400–700 THB per person and last 1.5–2 hours. Book in the morning to secure a spot. This is a great opportunity for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Travel back to the mainland or to a new destination (e.g., Krabi, Phuket, or Hua Hin). Take the morning ferry and enjoy the scenery during the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at your next destination. Check into a mid-range hotel and freshen up. Explore the local area — visit a famous beach, temple, or town center.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a famous night market in the new city (e.g., Krabi Town Walking Street or Phuket Old Town Night Market). Spend 2–3 hours eating, shopping, and soaking in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the island guesthouse before checkout
meals.lunch: Ferry snacks or a quick meal at the pier — grilled corn, spring rolls, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Night market feast — try 5–6 different dishes from various stalls including Hoi Tod (crispy oyster pancake), Khanom Krok (coconut pancakes), and fresh fruit skewers (budget 200–350 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage manageable for ferry and land transfers. Store large bags at the hotel and carry a day bag. October evenings can be warm and humid — dress light and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a famous local landmark — a temple complex, big Buddha, or cultural heritage site depending on your location. Hire a local guide for deeper context (500–800 THB for a 2-hour tour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a famous beach or bay for an afternoon of swimming and sunbathing. If in Krabi, visit Railay Beach via longtail boat. If in Phuket, head to Kata or Kamala Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Thai dinner show or Muay Thai boxing event for an authentic cultural experience. Many venues offer dinner packages combined with the show.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café — try Khanom Jeen (fermented rice noodles with curry) for a true local experience
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant — fresh seafood platter, papaya salad, and cold coconut water
meals.dinner: Thai dinner show venue — set menu with multiple courses including appetizers, main dishes, and dessert (600–900 THB per person including show)

day_by_day.notes: Book Muay Thai or dinner show tickets in advance. Dress modestly when visiting temples — cover shoulders and knees. Longtail boat to Railay Beach costs around 100–150 THB per person.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — spend the morning at your favorite beach discovered during the trip. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax. Take photos and soak in the last full day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Go on a final street food walking tour — either self-guided or with a local food tour guide. Visit 4–5 key street food spots and try dishes you haven't eaten yet during the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant. Celebrate the end of a wonderful trip with a special meal and perhaps a bottle of Thai wine or a cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Beach café — açaí bowl, fresh fruit platter, and a strong Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Street food tour bites — Boat noodles, Kanom Buang (crispy Thai crepes), grilled squid, and fresh-cut fruit
meals.dinner: Upscale Thai restaurant — 3-course meal with Tom Yum soup, Panang curry with jasmine rice, and sticky rice with durian or mango for dessert (600–900 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to buy any remaining souvenirs — Thai silk scarves, spices, chili pastes, and handmade jewelry make great gifts. Start packing in the evening to prepare for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a slow walk, meditate, or just sit and absorb the beauty of Thailand one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (standard checkout by 12:00 PM). Store luggage with the hotel if needed. Do any last-minute shopping or revisit a favorite café or restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport for your departure flight. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before your flight. Enjoy a final Thai meal at the airport before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a beloved local spot — enjoy your favorite Thai breakfast dish one last time
meals.lunch: Casual lunch near the hotel before checkout — light noodle soup or a sandwich from a bakery
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or food court — try a final bowl of Tom Yum noodles or a green curry before flying home

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and check-in online 24 hours before departure. Keep snacks and small Thai treats in your carry-on for the flight. Declare any food items at customs when returning home. Sawasdee kha/khrap — farewell Thailand!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon check-in, enjoy a welcome drink and a brief resort orientation. Settle into your beachfront suite and unwind after your journey.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome snack platter and chilled beverages arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority. Confirm early check-in availability if connecting from a long-haul flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a slow, luxurious start to your trip. Take a sunrise stroll along the private beachfront of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a full resort breakfast with panoramic sea views from the beachfront terrace restaurant.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach strip and nearby coastal promenade. Hire a private longtail boat for a personalized 2-hour coastal tour of nearby hidden coves and limestone formations. Return to the resort for a dip in the infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beach bar. Enjoy a curated Thai tasting menu at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring dishes like tom kha gai, massaman lamb, and mango sticky rice with gold leaf.

meals.breakfast: Resort's beachfront breakfast buffet with à la carte options — fresh tropical fruits, congee, eggs benedict, and freshly brewed Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside dining — grilled tiger prawns, papaya salad, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Signature Thai tasting menu at the resort's fine-dining restaurant — 5-course dinner with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Use Day 2 to acclimatize to the timezone and tropical heat. Stay hydrated and apply reef-safe sunscreen before any water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided snorkeling excursion to a nearby coral reef. Board a luxury speedboat for a half-day trip to a secluded snorkeling spot teeming with marine life. Includes equipment, a marine guide, and onboard refreshments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local floating market accessible by private longtail boat. Browse fresh produce, handmade crafts, and authentic street food stalls from the comfort of a wooden boat. Pick up local spices and artisan souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a traditional Thai massage at the resort spa. Enjoy a candlelit beachside dinner under the stars — a private table set up on the sand with personalized menu selections.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast butler service — freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit platter, and Thai iced tea
meals.lunch: Street food feast at the floating market — pad krapow, grilled satay skewers, mango with sticky rice, and fresh sugarcane juice
meals.dinner: Private beachside candlelit dinner — lobster thermidor, green curry with jasmine rice, and lychee panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkeling excursion and private beachside dinner 24 hours in advance through the resort's concierge. October weather may bring occasional short rain showers — have a backup indoor dining plan.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early on a private chartered speedboat for a full-day island-hopping adventure. First stop: a secluded uninhabited island with pristine white sand and crystal-clear water. Enjoy swimming, kayaking, and beachcombing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping to a second island known for its dramatic sea caves and emerald lagoons. Explore by kayak through sea caves and natural archways. Onboard gourmet picnic lunch served on the boat deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and head out to a nearby upscale beach club for sundowner cocktails. Dine at a highly regarded local seafood restaurant known for its fresh catch and Thai-fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — smoked salmon bagels, acai bowls, and cold brew coffee to fuel the day
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the chartered boat — charcuterie board, fresh sushi rolls, tropical fruits, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Premium seafood dinner at a local fine-dining restaurant — whole grilled barramundi, tom yum seafood soup, and coconut ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Full-day island hopping requires an early 7:00 AM departure. Pack reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a waterproof bag. The chartered boat includes a crew, snorkeling gear, and a cooler with beverages.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga session on the resort's beachfront deck led by a private instructor. Follow with a guided meditation and breathwork session. Afterward, explore the resort's tropical garden and beachfront at leisure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Thai cooking class hosted at a luxury culinary studio nearby. Learn to prepare 4 traditional Thai dishes including pad thai, green curry, som tum, and mango sticky rice. Take home a recipe booklet as a keepsake.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class for a private dinner set up in your suite or on a private terrace. Pair with a curated selection of Thai craft cocktails and mocktails.

meals.breakfast: Healthy resort breakfast — smoothie bowls, granola with coconut yogurt, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the cooking class venue — Thai spring rolls, fresh herb salads, and iced lemongrass tea
meals.dinner: Enjoy your own culinary creations from the cooking class served as a private suite dinner with cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 3–4 hours. Confirm dietary restrictions with the instructor in advance. A great activity for a rest day that still offers cultural immersion.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat transfer to a nearby iconic island (such as Phi Phi or Koh Lanta depending on resort location). Arrive early to beat crowds and explore the viewpoint for panoramic island vistas. Stroll through the charming village streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island's beaches — rent a private longtail boat to access quieter stretches of sand. Snorkel in the bay, spot tropical fish, and relax on a sun lounger at a premium beach club.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at the island's most celebrated fine-dining restaurant with views over the bay. Try signature dishes of the island's culinary scene. Return to resort by private speedboat transfer under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — continental spread with Thai-style congee and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch on the island — grilled seafood platter, tropical salads, and frozen cocktails
meals.dinner: Fine-dining island restaurant — tasting menu with local seafood, Thai herbs, and artisan desserts

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 8:00 AM to make the most of the island day. Private speedboat transfers can be arranged through the resort concierge. Carry cash for small local vendors on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Full spa day begins with a 90-minute traditional Thai herbal compress massage at the resort spa. Follow with a rejuvenating facial and body scrub treatment using local ingredients like turmeric and coconut.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the resort's infinity pool with a curated selection of books, music, and poolside service. Enjoy a private cabana experience with dedicated butler service, chilled towels, and premium beverages.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local street food tour led by a private guide. Explore the nearby town's night market on foot, sampling authentic Thai street food from renowned local vendors — a perfect contrast to resort fine dining.

meals.breakfast: Spa breakfast — light, nourishing options including fresh fruit, herbal teas, and whole grain toast with avocado
meals.lunch: Poolside cabana dining — club sandwiches, fresh spring rolls, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Street food tour dinner — moo ping (grilled pork skewers), khao man gai, pad see ew, roti with condensed milk, and fresh fruit shakes at various market stalls

day_by_day.notes: Book spa treatments at least 2 days in advance. The street food tour is best enjoyed with an empty stomach — skip heavy snacks before heading out. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the market tour.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private longtail boat tour to watch local fishermen at work in the bay. Visit a traditional fishing village to learn about the local way of life. Photography opportunity with stunning coastal backdrops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort and enjoy a private stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) session along the coastline. Alternatively, try kayaking through mangrove channels with a guided naturalist for an eco-immersive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive resort chef's table experience — a bespoke 7-course tasting menu prepared tableside by the head chef, featuring the finest local and imported ingredients, paired with premium Thai wines and international selections.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the boat tour — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee to go
meals.lunch: Resort restaurant lunch upon return — tom kha soup, green mango salad, and grilled chicken satay
meals.dinner: Chef's table 7-course tasting menu — signature dishes showcasing the best of Thai and international fusion cuisine with sommelier wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The chef's table experience must be reserved well in advance and may require a minimum spend. Dress code is smart casual. This is a highlight dining experience of the entire trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby national marine park (such as Mu Ko Lanta or Ang Thong Marine Park). Depart by private speedboat and explore pristine islands, hidden lagoons, and untouched beaches within the protected park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel or dive at the marine park's most spectacular reef sites. The private boat includes a certified dive guide for those who wish to scuba dive. Enjoy a floating picnic lunch anchored in a calm bay.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxed evening — cocktails on your private balcony watching the sunset, followed by a casual dinner at the resort's beachside grill.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs your way, fresh-pressed juices, and Thai-style rice porridge
meals.lunch: Floating picnic on the boat — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, sushi rolls, and chilled drinks
meals.dinner: Resort beachside grill — grilled whole snapper, garlic butter prawns, grilled corn, and tropical fruit sorbet

day_by_day.notes: Marine park entry fees are typically included in the private boat charter. Bring waterproof camera equipment or rent an underwater camera through the resort. October may bring some choppier seas — check conditions the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Cultural morning: visit a nearby Buddhist temple (wat) with a private guide. Learn about Thai Buddhist traditions, observe morning alms-giving ceremonies, and explore ornate temple architecture and grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby upscale town or resort area for boutique shopping — local silk, handmade jewelry, Thai art, and premium wellness products. Stop for an afternoon coffee at a stylish local café.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on a private chartered catamaran. Sip champagne as the sun dips below the horizon over the Andaman Sea. Arrive back at the resort pier for a late dinner at the resort's rooftop restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the temple visit — light continental spread and Thai iced coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a renowned local restaurant in town — khao soi (northern Thai curry noodles), larb salad, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant dinner — panoramic sea views, premium wagyu beef salad, seafood pad thai, and black sesame ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for temple visits — cover shoulders and knees. Carry a light scarf or sarong. The sunset catamaran cruise typically runs 2 hours and should be booked through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final island-hopping adventure — a curated 'best of' day combining your favorite spots from the trip. Revisit a beloved beach or snorkeling site, or explore a new hidden gem recommended by the resort's local guides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort by early afternoon. Indulge in a final spa treatment — a 60-minute aromatherapy massage to relax before the journey home. Spend remaining time at the pool or beach.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's most prestigious restaurant. A personalized menu is curated with the chef based on your preferences discovered throughout the stay. Toast to an unforgettable journey.

meals.breakfast: Special resort breakfast in bed — full Thai breakfast with congee, dim sum, fresh fruits, and premium teas
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch — fresh spring rolls, tom yum broth, and tropical fruit platter
meals.dinner: Personalized farewell tasting menu — chef's selection of your favorite dishes from the trip, with a complimentary dessert and sparkling wine toast

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout procedures and luggage storage options with the front desk. If departing the next morning, arrange a wake-up call and early breakfast service.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Take one last sunrise walk along the beach. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort. Pack up and check out — luggage can be stored with the concierge while you enjoy remaining hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration of the local area — revisit a favorite café, pick up final souvenirs, or simply sit at a beachside spot and soak in the atmosphere. Visit a local dessert shop for Thai sweets to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to the airport or onward destination. If time permits before departure, enjoy a final Thai meal at a celebrated airport lounge or nearby restaurant en route.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — your favorite items from the trip, ordered à la carte
meals.lunch: Local café or restaurant near the resort — khao man gai, fresh papaya salad, and Thai iced tea
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or a quick upscale meal at a nearby restaurant before departure transfer

day_by_day.notes: Check airline baggage allowances if you've purchased souvenirs or artisan goods. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before an international flight. Keep all valuables and documents in your carry-on.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — in transit or arriving home. Reflect on the incredible 13-day Thailand journey. If there is a long layover, explore an airport lounge for premium dining, showers, and relaxation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue travel or arrive at final destination. Unpack and begin settling back into routine with memories of Thailand's beaches, islands, and street food to last a lifetime.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive home or at final destination. Rest and recover from travel. Organize photos, review experiences, and begin planning a return trip to Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Airport lounge breakfast or in-flight premium meal service
meals.lunch: In-flight dining or airport lounge lunch during layover
meals.dinner: In-flight premium dinner service or home-cooked meal upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Day 13 is a travel and transition day. Keep it flexible. Ensure all receipts, travel documents, and customs declarations are organized. Consider travel insurance claims if any disruptions occurred during the trip.
